I will keep my land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits the local weather, the water conditions, and the way I know how to farm. At my age, I will not make the year more complicated than it needs to be. I will finish out the winter wheat that is already on the land, manage it steadily with moderate fertilizer, three irrigations, and a couple of pesticide sprays if pressure shows up, and then I will harvest it and go straight into summer maize. For the maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable production, and I will plant it with no-tillage after wheat harvest to save labor and keep moisture. I will not split the farm into many small crops because that adds work, raises risk, and makes management harder for me. I would rather run one familiar double-cropping system well than chase something uncertain.
